name: memory__create_entities
description: Create multiple new entities in the knowledge graph. An entity whose name already exists, or repeats an earlier entity in the same call, is skipped and its observations are not added; the result lists the skipped names in `skipped`. Use add_observations to add observations to an existing entity.

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

name: memory__create_relations
description: Create multiple new relations between entities in the knowledge graph. Relations should be in active voice

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

name: memory__add_observations
description: Add new observations to existing entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity to add the observations to

contents.description: An array of observation contents to add

name: memory__delete_entities
description: Delete multiple entities and their associated relations from the knowledge graph

entityNames.description: An array of entity names to delete

name: memory__delete_observations
description: Delete specific observations from entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity containing the observations

observations.description: An array of observations to delete

name: memory__delete_relations
description: Delete multiple relations from the knowledge graph

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

relations.description: An array of relations to delete

name: memory__read_graph
description: Read the entire knowledge graph: every entity with its observations, and every relation. The result grows with the graph, so use this only when you need everything; prefer search_nodes to find entities by keyword and open_nodes to read entities whose names you know.

entityTypes.description: Return only entities whose entityType is one of these (exact match), and only the relations that touch one of them. Omit to return every entity.

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

name: memory__search_nodes
description: Search the knowledge graph for entities whose name, type or observations contain the query (case-insensitive). Use this when you have a keyword, a topic or part of a name but not the exact entity names. Prefer open_nodes when you already know the exact names, and use read_graph only when you need the whole graph. Returns the matching entities and every relation that touches one of them.

query.description: The search query to match against entity names, types, and observation content

limit.description: Return at most this many matching entities (the first matches, in stored order), with the relations that touch them. Omit to return every match.

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.

name: memory__open_nodes
description: Retrieve specific entities by their exact names, with every relation that touches one of them. Use this when you already know the names (from the conversation, or from an earlier search_nodes or read_graph result); it is the cheapest way to read entities you can name. Prefer search_nodes when you only have a keyword or part of a name. Names that do not exist are skipped.

names.description: An array of entity names to retrieve

observationLimit.description: Return at most this many observations per entity (the first ones, in the order they were added) and add each entity's total as observationCount. Use 0 for names, types and counts only: a cheap overview of a large graph, after which open_nodes reads the entities you need in full. Omit to return every observation.
